einzeiler: A deep dive into J.M. Coetzee's complex novel Elizabeth Costello with novelist Mary…
kurzfassung: Recorded live at the Galway International Arts Festival, the hosts and guest novelist Mary Costello discuss J.M. Coetzee's enigmatic and challenging book Elizabeth Costello. They explore the novel's themes of animal rights, the limits of art, the problem of evil, and Coetzee's distinct literary style. The conversation also touches upon other works by Coetzee and how the book reflects the heavy burdens of authorship and fame.
stichpunkte: Live recording at the Galway International Arts Festival in front of an audience.
Guest novelist Mary Costello explains why J.M. Coetzee's Elizabeth Costello has been a lifelong favorite.
Discussion of the novel's unique structure consisting of eight linked lectures or lessons.
Analysis of Elizabeth Costello's uncompromising stance on animal cruelty and the meat industry.
Exploration of the chapter concerning the problem of evil and the controversy around writing about historical atrocities.
Examination of the blurring lines between authorial intent and fictional proxy in Coetzee's work.
Reading of powerful passages from the novel, including the harrowing airport car scene.
Reflections on Coetzee's memoir trilogy and his complex relationship with his mother and his own writing process.

clips.hook: An Irish name written by a South African about an Australian
clips.text: The guest explains that despite the familiar Irish surname in the title, the book was actually written by a South African author about an Australian fictional novelist.

clips.hook: The structural flaw in contemporary Euro-American fiction
clips.text: A quoted passage from a novel argues that modern literature relies on ignoring the actual lived realities of ordinary people.

clips.hook: Comparing the treatment of animals to the Holocaust
clips.text: The discussion turns to how the protagonist causes outrage by drawing a direct parallel between industrial slaughterhouses and Nazi concentration camps.

clips.hook: Writing is industry, not beauty or consolation
clips.text: In an archival clip, the author describes the act of writing as hard physical and mental work rather than a comforting or inherently beautiful pursuit.

beschreibung:
Recorded live in Galway in 2021, we were joined by novelist Mary Costello for a special episode recorded live at Galway International Arts Festival in Ireland. The book we're debating is Elizabeth Costello (2003) by South-African born Nobel Laureate J.M. Coetzee, a novel that politely asks the reader to consider, amongst other matters, animal rights, the power of faith and the limits of fiction itself. Also in this episode, books by two Irish authors: Sally Rooney's novel Beautiful World, Where Are You and John Moriarty’s The Hut at the Edge of the Village, a collection edited by Martin Shaw and published by the Lilliput Press.
